market_name: Will 1 Fed rate cut happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the implied probability move persists or was a thin-liquidity blip; cross-check 2y/10y yields and fed funds futures.
time_plan.1h: Confirm TLT direction aligns with the dovish read; look for any FOMC-speak or data release that explains the shift.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether rate-cut repricing is holding across the curve or fading.
time_plan.6h: Compare against SOFR/fed funds futures move to validate the leak hypothesis.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate whether TLT closed in the predicted direction and whether magnitude was material; log calibration.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a 2026 Fed rate cut signals a more dovish rate path. Lower expected policy rates pull down the front-to-belly of the curve and support long-duration bond prices. TLT is the most liquid, broadly-traded proxy for that duration exposure. However, a 'will at least 1 cut happen in 2026' market is likely already priced near-certain, so any incremental information content is small and the mapping to a large 12h move is weak.

time_plan.30m: Verify the probability move is real and check DXY spot reaction.
time_plan.1h: Cross-check EURUSD and rate-differential moves for consistency with dollar weakness.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether dollar softness is sustained or noise.
time_plan.6h: Compare to Treasury yield move for internal consistency.

predictions.reasoning: A more dovish Fed rate-cut expectation typically narrows US rate differentials and weighs on the dollar. UUP is a liquid DXY proxy. The linkage is directionally sound but weak over a 12h window, and a near-certain 'at least 1 cut' market carries little marginal information, so the expected move is small.

evidence_used: Market question on number of 2026 Fed 25bp rate cuts (at-least-1 strike)
Standard transmission: dovish rate expectations lower yields, support bonds, weaken USD
Liquidity of TLT and UUP as rate/FX proxies
uncertainty_notes: An 'at least 1 cut in 2026' market is probably already near-certain, giving minimal incremental signal
Direction of the anomaly (dovish vs hawkish repricing) is unknown; assumed rising cut probability = dovish
12h window is far too short to produce the 700bps tradable threshold from a probability shift
Bonds and USD respond to many macro drivers that can swamp this signal

llm_justification.summary: This market tracks whether the Fed delivers at least one 2026 rate cut. A sharp rise in the implied probability would read as a dovish shift, favoring long-duration Treasuries (TLT up) and a weaker dollar (UUP down). But the strike is likely already priced near-certain, the transmission is diffuse, and no realistic 12h move reaches the 700bps tradable bar. Treat as a low-confidence, non-tradable directional lean.
key_assumptions: The observed anomaly is a rise in cut probability (dovish)
Standard rate-transmission channels hold over the short window
TLT and UUP adequately proxy duration and dollar exposure
failure_modes: Market already near 100%, so no real information leaks and no move occurs
Move reverses as a liquidity blip on a thin Polymarket contract
Hawkish rather than dovish repricing, flipping both directions
Macro news (data, other central banks, risk sentiment) dominates bond and FX moves, overwhelming the signal
Magnitude far below tradable threshold, making the mapping economically irrelevant
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
